protocol.py: 4 biology problems (1 error, 1 warning, 2 notes).

1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 12 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at
least)
   line 103:  p300.aspirate(12, component_block["A3"])
   At line 103 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 12 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul. A
   pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and
   the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells:
   well A3 in slot 4.
   Affected: well A3 in slot 4.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [352f94cde52a]

2. WARNING MIX-BEFORE-DRAW: Liquid drawn from well A1 in slot 5 before it was mixed: added
at line 104, drawn at line 126
   line 104:  p300.dispense(12, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 104 liquid was added to well A1 in slot 5, which already held a different liquid.
   At line 126 liquid was drawn out of it again, and the well was never mixed in between.
   Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the tip drew is not
   at the concentration you calculated. In a dilution series every later step inherits the
   error.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 5.
   Also reached 46 other wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 38 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix the well after the addition at line 104: `mix_after=(5, volume)` in a transfer,
   or `pipette.mix(5, volume, well)`. Integra suggests about 5 cycles at about 80% of the
   volume in the well.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Svec et al. 2015: how good is a PCR efficiency estimate
           https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4822216/
   [3b44fb78e28c]

3. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 46 wells of dntp and polymerase with a
sample
   line 127:  p300.dispense(23, reaction_well)
   At line 127 the robot starts putting dntp and polymerase into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL
   PCR Full Skirt (slot 3), and 46 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on
   this plate holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a
   reagent is contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal
   and nothing on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5,
   A6, A7, A8 and 38 more in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 38 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 0.75 ul of dntp and polymerase and 2 ul of water
   in place of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [e7ae0b97baa3]

4. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 46 wells never mixed after template 1, template 2, template 3,
template 4 and 42 more went in (8% of the well)
   line 134:  p20.dispense(2, reaction_well)
   At line 134 the robot added template 1, template 2, template 3, template 4 and 42 more to
   wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 38 more in slot 3, which already held buffer,
   dntp, fwd primer, rev primer and 2 more (this line did it 46 times). The addition was 8%
   of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two
   liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at
   the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before
   cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 38 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 38 more in slot 3 after line 134:
   `mix_after=(5, 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [6922a133c5fc]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
